chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, from Al-Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is disliked that the one in Ihram should sleep upon a yellow bed or upon a yellow bed-spread.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The one in Ihram (a pilgrim in the sacred state)
key_terms.كُرِهَ: Disliked (a legal ruling indicating preference against an action, but not forbidden)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sleeping on yellow bedding while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies the *karahat* (dislike) of a pilgrim in Ihram sleeping on yellow bedding, reflecting the scholarly tradition that Ihram entails a state of ritual distinctiveness and modesty. While some jurists debate whether this applies to the color itself or the fabric's texture, it underscores the aesthetic and spiritual purity required during the sacred rites of Hajj and Umrah.
